anya: Heads-up — I want to propose a concise set of 'service qualification' gates we can use to decide GA for the new inference routing features. Not just SLA + docs — also commercial exit/fallback rules and billing transparency.

mike: +1. can you sketch the gates?

anya: Sketch below. Aim is a go/no-go checklist we can show PMs & sales before final signoff. We'll need owners for each item.

joel: Nice. make sure the runtime side has a clear fallback matrix (which model/region/plan we fallback to) and cost delta communicated to customers.

anya: Agreed. rough gates (for discussion):
- SLA: 99.95% availability for hosted endpoints, <150ms p50 gen on standard models, p95 <500ms for common routes.
- Docs: Quickstart + migration guide + troubleshooting KB with at least 8 common errors and exact remediation steps.
- Monitoring: Per-route latency + error-rate dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, alerting for SLO burn >10% for 3m.
- Support: SLA-backed customer response time (P1 1h, P2 4h), playbooks for throttling, surges, and capacity failovers.
- Pricing readiness: Public pricing page updated, per-route metering validated end-to-end, billing dispute playbook.
- Fallback/commercial exit: Defined fallback model variants, documented cost delta, and a contract-level escape hatch for enterprise customers.

sara: Can we make SLA numbers tighter for dedicated customers? e.g., 99.99% and p95 <250ms when pinned capacity?

anya: Yes — we can add tiered SLOs (hosted vs dedicated). I'll add an explicit line.

elaine: how do we validate docs completeness? last time we missed a CLI example and had onboarding dropoff.

mike: propose validation steps: internal runbook for new user flow with a paid test account + 3 sample apps (chat, embeddings, reranking) that must work end-to-end. docs considered complete if all 3 pass and PR reviews done by docs + eng.

joel: put this in a tiny checklist we can gate on the release ticket. i.e. QA task list must be green.

anya: I'll draft the checklist. quick SLO snippet for the doc:
```
SLOs (hosted):
- availability: 99.95% monthly
- latency gen (p50): <150ms
- latency gen (p95): <500ms
- error rate: <0.2% 5xx
SLOs (dedicated):
- availability: 99.99% monthly
- latency gen (p50): <120ms
- latency gen (p95): <250ms
- error rate: <0.1% 5xx
```

mike: Might want to add a token-throttling policy and explain how we meter burst vs sustained. That was a sticky point with pilot customers.

anya: Good call. Add an example billing scenario in the billing doc (e.g., customer runs 1MM tokens in 10s bursts, how billing shows up).

elaine: For monitoring, also include synthetic checks for typical prompts (chat warmup) to ensure KV-cache hits are reasonable.

joel: And a regression alert tied to prompt sets (if BLEU/semantic score drops >5% for control prompts, open an incident). PMs + research need that.

anya: I'll link to the eval harness.

release-bot: New draft checklist created: https://redwood.internal/s/REQ-9876 (assigned to anya) :white_check_mark:

mike: ownership proposals: SLA + routing fallback = joel; Docs + runbooks = elaine; Monitoring + alerts = sara; Billing + pricing = mike; Exec sign-off = anya.

elaine: I can take docs, will schedule a quick audit with UX and a migrations pass.

joel: I'll document the fallback matrix. question: do we allow automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized models or require explicit customer opt-in?

sara: For hosted, auto-fallback is allowed but must be signaled via response header and customer billing notice. For enterprise (private/dedicated) we require explicit opt-in.

mike: add a short customer-facing paragraph: "We may automatically route to alternative model variants during capacity constraints; you'll see a header + billing detail. For enterprise customers we will only do this with your consent."

anya: Excellent. final practical go/no-go heuristics I'd like to propose: all critical checkboxes green + 2-week pilot with two anchor customers, no P1 incidents in pilot week, and billing audit complete.

joel: sounds reasonable. can we shorten pilot to 1 week if both pilots are internal partners?

anya: Possibly — will flag that as an exception and require added monitoring sensitivity.

sara: timeline?

anya: Draft checklist and owners by EOD tomorrow. Pilot scheduling target: next Mon. Final signoff call on Thurs.

mike: I'll prep the billing scenario docs and a sample invoice snapshot.

elaine: I'll start the docs audit and ping UX.

joel: I'll post the fallback matrix here when ready.

anya: Thanks team. tagging execs once checklist is green. :rocket:
